image_description: A close-up, cropped view of a light blue ring binder. The image focuses on the spine area (left) showing black binding material and two silver metal rings holding white paper. The main body is a smooth, light blue plastic or vinyl cover with a clear plastic pocket on the right side containing a white insert. The perspective is tight, cutting off the top and bottom of the binder.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The metal rings appear to merge into the paper without clear punch holes. The geometry of the rings is slightly distorted; they look like flattened loops rather than cylindrical wire, and the connection point to the spine mechanism is undefined/melted.
The edge of the clear pocket on the right has a soft, glowing halo rather than a sharp refractive edge typical of plastic. It blends too smoothly into the blue background.
The black spine texture looks smudged and lacks the detailed grain or stitching usually found on binder spines. It appears as a flat black gradient rather than a physical object.

To check if the rings are closed loops and properly separated from the paper and spine.

To assess the realism of the lighting and material textures (plastic vs. metal).

focus_areas: Integrity of the metal ring mechanism (are they closed loops?)
Interaction between rings and paper (are there punch holes?)
Refraction and edges of the clear plastic pocket

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the metal rings. In AI images, these often fail to form complete circles or merge with the paper. Check if the 'holes' in the paper are actually rendered or if the rings just sit on top. Also, verify if the clear pocket looks like a separate layer or just a painted highlight.
